Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

siege noun

also besiege, besiege a town, blockade, under siege, hold out (a siege), raise the siege, starve into surrender, send relief

classical

Cic. Mur. 20: partim vī, partim obsidiōne urbēs capere (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 187

obsidiō, obsidiōnis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a siege, a blockade

Other words

  • obsideō, obsidēre, obsēdī, obsessum — besiege, blockade

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. obsideō II; Traupman 186: oppidum obsidēre · Conjugation on Wiktionary

Examples

  • oppidum obsidēre

    to besiege a townTraupman 186

  • Oppidum obsidiōnem quattuor mēnsēs sustinuit.

    The town held out for four months.Traupman 187

  • obsidiōnem tolerāre

    to hold out against a siegeTac. Hist. 1.33 (Lewis & Short)

  • oppidum obsidiōne līberāre

    to raise the siege on a townTraupman 187

  • obsidiōnem solvere

    to bring a siege to an end (by surrender or relief)Lewis & Short s.v. obsidiō

  • oppidum famē domāre

    to starve a town into surrenderTraupman 188

  • oppidum oppugnāre

    to storm a townTraupman 188

  • subsidium alicui summittere

    to send relief to someoneTraupman 188; cf. Caes. BG 2.6 (Lewis & Short s.v. summittō)

See also capture, attack, surrender, war.

SourcesLewis & Short: obsidio · Lewis & Short: obsideo · Lewis & Short: summitto

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 186–188, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
